evidence.observation: The eight new records have stable IDs, canonical paths, explicit review metadata, typed relations, and bounded canonical references; narrower artifact-authorship, oral-history, rights, private-bridge, and unresolved-event work remains in the wanted queue.

The pages distinguish native documents, authenticated platform controls, public reporting, institutional program descriptions, protected packet review, participant photographs, attributed memory, and failed archive access rather than blending them into one evidence class.

Chronology, recurring method, project afterlife, individual role, scene, place, testimony, and protected absence remain distinct editorial objects; a vivid scene is not promoted into role, attendance, impact, or sole-authorship proof.
The new records resolve to current canonical claim and inquiry IDs, ordinary relative links, and source-reencounter methods without creating a competing source or claim registry.
The system separates not recovered, located-not-read, protected, rights-blocked, collectively unresolved, attributed, intentionally absent, mature-but-unselected, and publicly projected states.

The project pages now connect Open House and Water Publics to a longer artistic lineage, NYC Artist Coalition to events and participation infrastructure, and KC Spaces Fund to role and handoff records while preserving each project's own period and collaborators.

Both lineage pages reject simple causality; the event chronology preserves direct versus associated hosting and one unresolved control slot; the role map withholds artifact-level allocation pending collaborator review.

All eight new records have no allowed public surfaces, no public Wiki route was introduced, and protected media, private testimony, participant data, relationship graphs, and family details remain outside public projection.
